name: Congenital Absence of the Internal Carotid Artery

criteria.description: Complete absence or agenesis of the internal carotid artery confirmed by imaging
Presence of collateral cerebral circulation compensating for absent ICA
Neurological symptoms consistent with cerebral hypoperfusion or ischemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of absent internal carotid artery with evidence of collateral circulation; clinical symptoms supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities such as CT angiography or MR angiography.

imaging: Absence of internal carotid artery on CT angiography or MR angiography
Presence of collateral arterial pathways such as enlarged posterior communicating artery
Possible cerebral perfusion deficits on perfusion imaging
other: Clinical neurological examination may reveal focal deficits depending on ischemic areas

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of ICA vessel on imaging with abrupt occlusion
History of vascular risk factors or embolic events
Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography
Usually affects mid to distal ICA segments rather than complete absence

redFlags: Signs of cerebral aneurysm rupture such as sudden severe headache
references: Bouthillier A, et al. Congenital absence of the internal carotid artery: a review. Neurosurgery. 1991.
Lie TA. Congenital anomalies of the carotid arteries. Am J Roentgenol Radium Ther Nucl Med. 1968.
Orphanet: Congenital absence of the internal carotid artery (ORPHA:981)
